drives_non_pixel: This file's own imports are closure_NNPDF_truth.fit / closure_JAM_truth_small.fit / closure_NNPDF_truth_small.fit (plus jax.numpy/numpy/pytest; closure_JAM_truth.fit was imported too until the 2026-08-14 SUITES trim) -- no direct 'import pixel' anywhere in the file. Those four fit.py modules are what import pixel.api.analysis / pixel.core.model / pixel.core.params / pixel.priors, and it is that machinery (Analysis.tie, Model.tie, normalize_ties, apply_ties, parameter_table) this file actually exercises, reached only through each suite's _gp_prior/build_analysis rather than imported directly. Treated as pixel-adjacent, not purely non-pixel.

tests.name: test_one_amplitude_drives_both_mean_and_sigma
tests.claim: One amplitude drives both the prior mean and the kernel sigma.
tests.actual: Checks cfg.gp_mean(name)==cfg.gp_sigma(name)==cfg.gp_amplitude(name) (both gp_mean/gp_sigma are literally 'return gp_amplitude(field)', config.py:904-911) and that four retired constants (GP_MEAN_HIGH etc.) are absent.
tests.how: Pure cfg-level function calls; never touches _gp_prior, Parameter, or analysis.tie.
tests.catches: Reintroduction of the pre-tie four-separate-constants layout (hasattr loop). Catches nothing about _gp_prior's actual construction: repo-wide grep finds gp_mean/gp_sigma have no caller anywhere except config.py's own definitions and this test -- _gp_prior (fit.py:122) calls cfg.gp_amplitude directly.

tests.name: test_high_tier_is_singlet_gluon_charm
tests.claim: The high-amplitude tier is exactly {sigma, g, t15}; 9 fields total.
tests.actual: Computes the set of fields where gp_amplitude(n)==GP_AMPLITUDE_HIGH and compares to a hardcoded set; checks len(ALL_FIELDS)==9.
tests.how: cfg-level only; the expected set is the tier list documented in config.py's own HIGH_PRIOR_FIELDS comment.
tests.catches: HIGH_PRIOR_FIELDS gaining/losing a field, or ALL_FIELDS changing count. Says nothing about whether 5.0/1.0 are the physically right amplitudes.

tests.name: test_gp_prior_starts_at_a_plus_minus_a
tests.claim: The GP prior built by _gp_prior starts at a +- a (mean == sd == amplitude).
tests.actual: Builds prior = suite._gp_prior(name) directly (never calls build_analysis/analysis.tie) and checks prior_mean(nodes)==amplitude and sqrt(diag(prior_cov(nodes)))==amplitude, both read once, at construction.
tests.how: mean and sd both trace to the single cfg.gp_amplitude(name) call inside _gp_prior (fit.py:122-135); no tie is ever attached in this code path.
tests.catches: A transcription bug where _gp_prior passes different values to Const vs LogRBF's sigma. Catches nothing about a missing or broken analysis.tie: demonstrated by mutation (see measurements) that these exact assertions pass unchanged when the tie is never attached at all; test_build_ties_mean_to_sigma below is the test that actually would catch that.

tests.name: test_build_ties_mean_to_sigma
tests.claim: analysis.tie(mean.N, to=cov.sigma), as wired into build_analysis, actually keeps mean following sigma.
tests.actual: Builds a real Model via build_analysis; checks len(model.ties)==9 and n_free==0; for each field checks parameter_table()'s tied_to string, then calls apply_parameter_overrides to set cov.sigma to moved=3.7 (neither tier value) and reads mean/sd back from the rebuilt model's prior, asserting both now read 3.7.
tests.how: apply_parameter_overrides reconstructs Model (_with_theta -> __init__), which reruns pixel.core.params.normalize_ties/apply_ties (model.py:1036-1037) -- the same code ravel's rebuild runs under jit/grad. This is a real post-move readback, not a construction-time coincidence.
tests.bar: rtol 1e-12 (mean), rtol 1e-9 (sd); exact len()/== on ties/n_free
tests.catches: A dropped analysis.tie(...) call (len(model.ties) would be 0), a tie declared to the wrong source/target, or apply_ties/normalize_ties failing to propagate a moved value through a full Model rebuild. Confirmed by source reading of Model.__init__ (ties defaults to (), no identity-based auto-tie-detection exists) that a dropped tie call is caught here, not silently passed.

tests.name: test_nuisance_fields_are_not_tied
tests.claim: Lattice-systematic nuisance fields are never tied; their zero-mean prior has no mean parameter to tie.
tests.actual: Builds a real Model via build_analysis(mode='lattice'); for every model field not in cfg.ALL_FIELDS, checks no tied_to selector starts with its prefix and no prior.mean selector exists for it. Skips entirely if the suite registers zero nuisance fields.
tests.bar: exact membership/prefix check; skip if no nuisance fields
tests.catches: The physical-field tie loop in build_analysis over-matching a nuisance selector, or _nuisance_prior's Zero mean growing an accidental Parameter. 2 of 4 parametrized suites (small_jam, small_nnpdf) always pytest.skip: neither _small config.py defines nuisance_specs, confirmed by grep, so only full_jam/full_nnpdf run real assertions here.

tests.name: test_prior_stays_fully_fixed
tests.claim: The tie does not add a sampled hyper-parameter; the prior is fully fixed.
tests.actual: Asserts suite.cfg.N_HYPERPARAMS==0 and suite.cfg.FROZEN_COV_PARAMS==('sigma','length','x_reg'). No Model is built.
tests.how: Two literal comparisons against cfg constants; N_HYPERPARAMS reduces to 0 unconditionally whenever GP_AMPLITUDE_FREE is False, by the ternary that defines it.
tests.bar: exact equality (==) on two cfg constants
tests.catches: A new cov parameter added without extending FROZEN_COV_PARAMS, or GP_AMPLITUDE_FREE's default flipped without updating the derived count. Declaration-only: test_build_ties_mean_to_sigma's model.n_free==0 is the corresponding outcome check on a real compiled model.

tests.name: test_amplitude_is_frozen_and_unpenalised_by_default
tests.claim: By default the tied amplitude is frozen and carries no hyper-prior, so the evidence is unshifted.
tests.actual: Calls suite._gp_prior(name).cov.sigma directly (bypasses build_analysis) and checks .frozen is True, .prior is None, .bounds == (GP_AMPLITUDE_FLOOR, None).
tests.how: Parameter-metadata structural check on _gp_prior's own construction logic, which is appropriately where this property lives (does not need the tie/build_analysis machinery).
tests.bar: exact equality/identity checks on Parameter metadata
tests.catches: _gp_prior losing the frozen=not cfg.GP_AMPLITUDE_FREE / prior=cfg.gp_amplitude_prior(field) wiring for the default (frozen) branch.

tests.name: test_floor_sits_strictly_below_every_starting_amplitude
tests.claim: GP_AMPLITUDE_FLOOR sits strictly below every field's starting amplitude, so the inverse-softplus transform stays finite.
tests.actual: Checks 0.9 < GP_AMPLITUDE_FLOOR < 1.0, and per field that gp_amplitude(name) > GP_AMPLITUDE_FLOOR and that the closed-form inv_softplus(offset) is finite.
tests.how: inv_softplus(offset) = offset + log(-expm1(-offset)) is finite iff offset > 0 exactly, a closed-form numerical fact, evaluated directly.
tests.catches: GP_AMPLITUDE_FLOOR set at or above GP_AMPLITUDE_LOW (1.0), which sends eta to -inf for the low tier under the sampler's transform. The 0.9 lower literal itself is an unmeasured sanity range, not a derived bound.

tests.name: test_floating_attaches_the_floor_and_a_centred_hyper_prior
tests.claim: Floating GP_AMPLITUDE_FREE attaches the floor and a hyper-prior centred on each field's own tier value.
tests.actual: monkeypatches GP_AMPLITUDE_FREE=True; per field checks sigma.frozen is False, bounds unchanged, prior is not None, and neg2_logpdf at the tier value is below neg2_logpdf at 10x/0.1x; sums neg2_logpdf at centre over all 9 fields and checks the total against a hardcoded 13.7209.
tests.how: Structural (frozen/bounds/prior-not-None) + shape (centred-minimum ordering, true for any centred LogNormal at this sigma, so it mainly confirms log_center is per-field) + closed-form total.
tests.catches: log_center hardcoded to one tier instead of math.log(gp_amplitude(field)) (caught by the centred-minimum check, A2) or GP_AMPLITUDE_PRIOR_SIGMA changed without updating the literal (caught by the A1 total, independently verified against pixel.core.params.LogNormal.neg2_logpdf to 2.05e-06 relative -- see measurements). Weakest load-bearing part is the plain structural trio, hence F1/S3 as the primary code; the total is the strongest part of this test and is A1-grade.

tests.name: test_prior_and_accessors_all_follow_one_patched_amplitude
tests.claim: cfg.gp_amplitude is the single source: patch it and both accessors AND the built prior follow it, per field.
tests.actual: monkeypatches cfg.gp_amplitude to nine DISTINCT per-field probe values (2.5 + 0.37*i, asserted distinct from each other, from GP_AMPLITUDE_HIGH/LOW, and above GP_AMPLITUDE_FLOOR), then requires cfg.gp_mean(name), cfg.gp_sigma(name), float(_gp_prior(name).mean.N.value) and float(_gp_prior(name).cov.sigma.value) all to equal that field's probe EXACTLY.
tests.how: One patched source, four exact == per field. Separates DELEGATION from a hand-copied tier table (which every other check in the file accepts), pins that _gp_prior reads the accessor at call time rather than an import-time snapshot, and breaks the file's tier degeneracy -- gp_amplitude returns only 2 distinct values over 9 fields, so a within-tier cross-wire is invisible to every other test here.
tests.bar: exact ==; probe non-degeneracy asserted, not assumed
tests.catches: gp_mean/gp_sigma re-implementing the tier table instead of delegating to gp_amplitude (mutation gp_mean_duplicates_tier_table); _gp_prior inlining the tier table or snapshotting it at import instead of calling cfg.gp_amplitude (mutation gp_prior_inlines_tier_table); _gp_prior(name) reading another same-tier field's amplitude. Does NOT establish that gp_mean/gp_sigma have any production caller -- they have none; see weakness -02.

weaknesses.evidence: RESOLVED 2026-08-13 by test_one_amplitude_drives_both_mean_and_sigma. The two alias comparisons are kept (they still fail an alias hand-edit) but are no longer the whole check: the test now also requires the values that actually reach priors.Const and priors.LogRBF -- _gp_prior(name).mean.N.value and .cov.sigma.value -- to equal gp_mean(name)/gp_sigma(name) EXACTLY. The accessors therefore describe the prior that is built rather than their own body, and the exact `==` is strictly stronger than any other bar in the file. Acceptance: perturbing only the covariance amplitude in _gp_prior by 1e-11 relative (mut_ties.py MUT=sigma_epsilon, fit.py re-exec'd from mutated source) fails this test alone -- `assert 1.00000000001 == 1.0` at line 100 -- with the file's other 36 cases passing, including test_gp_prior_starts_at_a_plus_minus_a, whose rtol=1e-9 sd bar absorbs that same drift. Note this does not make gp_mean/gp_sigma non-orphaned; see -02. tests/test_closure_prior_ties.py:76-77 (assert cfg.gp_mean(name) == amplitude / assert cfg.gp_sigma(name) == amplitude) against closure_JAM_truth/config.py:904-911 (gp_mean and gp_sigma are each literally 'return gp_amplitude(field)')

Oracles: F1 for n_free, the free selector set, has_prior and tied_to; A1 for the bounds array (every lower bound at GP_AMPLITUDE_FLOOR, every upper inf) and for the gradient -- jax.grad through model._rebuild (the same closure ravel hands the sampler under jit) of sum_i mean.N_i**2 must return 2*sigma_i at every free coordinate, which is elementary calculus and the closure analogue of tests/test_parameter_ties.py::test_gradient_flows_through_the_tie_to_the_source. Measured: n_free 9, ties 9, x0 = [1, 1, 5, 5, 5, 1, 1, 1, 1], bounds lower 0.99 upper inf, max|grad/(2*x0) - 1| = 0.0 exactly. Acceptance: removing the freeze loop's `if attr == 'sigma' and cfg.GP_AMPLITUDE_FREE: continue` (mut_ties.py MUT=refreeze_sigma) fails it alone -- `assert 0 == 9` at line 382, 4 failed/36 passed -- and MUT=drop_tie fails it too. NOTE recorded in the test docstring: cfg.N_HYPERPARAMS is evaluated at import time from the module-level GP_AMPLITUDE_FREE, so monkeypatching the flag cannot move it; asserting n_free == N_HYPERPARAMS under a monkeypatch would have been a test that could only fail. n_free is compared to len(cfg.ALL_FIELDS) instead. closure_JAM_truth/fit.py:229-235 (build_analysis's freeze loop) contains 'if attr == "sigma" and cfg.GP_AMPLITUDE_FREE: continue', whose own comment says re-freezing here 'would silently override cfg.GP_AMPLITUDE_FREE'. No test in this file (or anywhere in tests/) calls build_analysis with GP_AMPLITUDE_FREE patched True: test_floating_attaches_the_floor_and_a_centred_hyper_prior only calls suite._gp_prior(name) directly, never build_analysis. So the actual integration point -- does the compiled Model really leave cov.sigma free (model.n_free == len(cfg.ALL_FIELDS), matching cfg.N_HYPERPARAMS) when floated, and does a real evidence gradient flow through the tie to the floated source the way test_parameter_ties.py::test_gradient_flows_through_the_tie_to_the_source proves for the toy fixture -- is untested for the closure suites specifically.

unjustified_tolerances.quantity: sum of LogNormal.neg2_logpdf at each field's own tier centre, over 9 fields
unjustified_tolerances.comment_added: Each per-field value is the closed form at its own centre (z=0): 2*log(a) + log(2*pi) + 2*log(sigma). rel=1e-4 covers the literal's 4-decimal rounding (measured 2.05e-06 actual), nothing looser.

measurements.claim: test_gp_prior_starts_at_a_plus_minus_a's assertions pass unchanged with no tie anywhere in the construction, and the same construction with sigma moved (no tie) leaves mean stale while sd tracks the move -- demonstrating the W-COMMON/W1 finding on that test by mutation.
measurements.command: python3 script mirroring _gp_prior's exact construction (priors.Const/priors.LogRBF/Parameter only, no closure_*/ import): build mean=Const(N=5.0), cov=LogRBF(sigma=Parameter(5.0)); read mean/sd (both 5.0); rebuild cov with sigma=Parameter(3.7) and mean left at Const(N=5.0); read mean/sd again. Separately, build a toy _GP/_Mean/_Cov eqx.Module pytree and run pixel.core.params.normalize_ties + ravel on it (the same functions Model.__init__ calls) to show the contrast when a real tie IS declared.
measurements.result: No tie: at construction mean[0]=5.0, sd[0]=5.00000000001 (test's check would pass). After moving sigma alone: mean[0]=5.0 (stale), sd[0]=3.700000000013514 -- diverged, a+-a broken, invisible to a construction-only re-check. With a real tie (P.normalize_ties + P.ravel, ties=(('mean.N','cov.sigma'),)): after moving the source to 3.7, mean.N=3.7, cov.sigma=3.7 -- correctly propagated. Also confirmed mean.N is cov.sigma is False even in the untied case (not even literal object-sharing, just independently seeded).

measurements.claim: test_floating_attaches_the_floor_and_a_centred_hyper_prior's hardcoded 13.7209 total is the closed-form LogNormal(log_center=log(a), sigma=0.5, loc=0).neg2_logpdf(a) at z=0, i.e. 2*log(a) + log(2*pi) + 2*log(sigma), not an unverifiable regression pin.
measurements.command: python3, importing pixel.core.params.LogNormal directly (no closure_*/ import): for a in (5.0, 1.0), compare float(LogNormal(log_center=math.log(a), sigma=0.5).neg2_logpdf(jnp.asarray(a))) against the hand closed form 2*math.log(a)+math.log(2*math.pi)+2*math.log(0.5); then total = 3*value(a=5) + 6*value(a=1).
measurements.result: a=5.0: code=3.6704585301576556 closed_form=3.6704585301576547 (diff 8.9e-16). a=1.0: code=0.45158270528945477 closed_form=identical (diff 0). total=13.720871822209695 vs the file's literal 13.7209, relative difference 2.054e-06 -- well inside the assertion's rel=1e-4 bar, consistent with a 4-decimal-rounded literal, not a loose bar.

measurements.claim: LogRBF's default 1e-10 diagonal jitter contributes a relative sd/mean deviation of 5.0e-11 at a=1.0, 2.0e-12 at a=5.0, and 3.65e-12 at a=3.7 (the values this file actually uses), all far under the rtol=1e-9 bars at lines 138 and 191.
measurements.command: python3 -c: for a in (1.0, 5.0, 3.7): dev = sqrt(1 + 1e-10/a**2) - 1; margin = 1e-9/dev
measurements.result: a=1.0: sd/mean=1.00000000005, dev=5.000e-11, margin=20.0x. a=5.0: sd/mean=1.000000000002, dev=2.000e-12, margin=500.0x. a=3.7: sd/mean=1.0000000000036522, dev=3.652e-12, margin=273.8x. The a=1.0 row matches guides/tying_parameters.md's own published table (1.00000000005) exactly.

measurements.command: for m in gp_mean_duplicates_tier_table gp_prior_inlines_tier_table; do MUT=$m OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 PYTHONPATH=scratchpad/mut_WA venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_closure_prior_ties.py -q -p no:randomly -p mut_ties_wa; done (serial, one at a time)
measurements.result: Both mutations give 4 failed / 39 passed -- ONLY the four test_prior_and_accessors_all_follow_one_patched_amplitude cases fail, and every other test in the file passes, including the three build_analysis tests. gp_prior_inlines_tier_table fails at line 204 with 'assert 1.0 == 2.5' (the prior's mean.N carries the inlined tier value instead of the patched amplitude), 21.82s. gp_mean_duplicates_tier_table fails at line 200 with cfg.gp_mean('t3') returning 1.0 against a probe of 2.5, 20.57s. After: mean.N = 2.0, cov.sigma = 2.0, tied_to = 'fields.q.prior.cov.sigma', frozen = True -- the declared 7.0 is discarded, not merely constrained. notes_for_readme: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-14 (owner's instruction): SUITES is now the NNPDF pair only, and the two JAM legs were removed as duplication. The original note read: 'test_closure_prior_ties.py's SUITES parametrization is 4 independently-maintained fit.py/config.py copies, not 4 physics variants of one code path -- worth stating in the area index so readers don't discount the x4 as redundant.' The reasoning that overrode it: nothing in this file reads the truth PDF set, so each JAM leg re-ran the identical normalize_ties/apply_ties path against a second copy of the same constants. What is genuinely given up is the per-copy drift guard on the two JAM config.py/fit.py files; small_jam is kept in _TIE_REBUILD_SUITES as the canary for it.
